title: Tenochtitlan
capsule: Tenochtitlan was the island capital of the Mexica, founded around 1325 on a marshy islet in Lake Texcoco in the Valley of Mexico after the migrant Mexica were expelled from Culhuacan and settled where, by tradition, they saw an eagle perched on a cactus. Through the fourteenth century the young city was a tributary client of the dominant Tepanec power at Azcapotzalco, supplying warriors to its ruler Tezozomoc; the Mexica obtained their first tlatoani, Acamapichtli, around 1372, followed by Huitzilihuitl and Chimalpopoca. After Tezozomoc's death the usurper Maxtla turned on Tenochtitlan, and under the tlatoani Itzcoatl the Mexica allied with Texcoco's Nezahualcoyotl and the dissident Tepanec city of Tlacopan to crush Azcapotzalco in 1428. This victory established the Aztec Triple Alliance around 1428–1430, transforming Tenochtitlan from a subordinate town into the seat of an expanding imperial confederation.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The city's footprint is archaeologically confirmed beneath central Mexico City; its political boundaries as a sovereign entity before Triple Alliance formation are less precisely delineated.
